title: Formal Urdu
tagline: The polite, ceremonial register: guests, elders, speeches.
canDo: You can switch into formal Urdu when the occasion calls for it

grammar.title: Honorific verbs
grammar.body: Formal Urdu replaces everyday verbs for the person you're honouring: aana → tashreef lana, baithna → tashreef rakhna, kehna → farmana, khana/peena → nosh farmana. Use them for others, never for yourself.

grammar.title: Izafat: the linking -e-
grammar.body: ism-e-shareef (noble name), wazir-e-azam (prime minister), dard-e-dil (pain of the heart). The -e- joins a noun to what describes or owns it. The -o- means 'and': khawateen-o-hazraat.

grammar.title: Raise them, lower yourself
grammar.body: Their home: daulat khana. Yours: ghareeb khana. Their speaking: farmana. Yours: arz karna. The grammar is ordinary; the word choice carries the respect.

teach.title: Formal Urdu swaps the verb
teach.info: Everyday: aaiye, baithiye, boliye, khaiye. Formal: tashreef laiye, tashreef rakhiye, farmaiye, nosh farmaiye. Same meaning, more ceremony. You'll hear it at weddings, on TV, and from anyone's grandfather.

teach.tip: Also what a shopkeeper says when you walk in: 'Ji, farmaiye?'
Only for someone else's eating. Nobody 'nosh farmaos' their own lunch.

teach.title: Raise them, lower yourself
teach.info: In formal Urdu the other person's things get grand words and yours get humble ones. Their home is a daulat khana (house of wealth). Yours is a ghareeb khana (poor house), even if it has a pool.

teach.title: The little -e-
teach.info: ism-e-shareef, 'name of nobility'. That -e- is the izafat: it links two words as 'X of Y' or 'Y X'. You know it already: Koh-e-Noor (mountain of light), Sher-e-Punjab, Wazir-e-Azam.

teach.tip: The joke about two nawabs of Lucknow: each said 'pehle aap' at the train door until the train left.

boss.title: Tea at Mrs. Butt's
boss.blurb: Formal drawing room. Good china. Mrs. Butt is grading your manners.
boss.scene: Ammi has sent you to drop off a wedding card. Mrs. Butt opens the door herself. The drawing room has plastic on the sofas and a clock shaped like Pakistan.

options.reaction: She did not expect 'aadaab' from someone your age. Points awarded.

end.title: Impeccable
end.text: You arrived, sat, sipped and left in formal Urdu. Mrs. Butt has already phoned three people to say how well brought up you are. This will have consequences.
